recent_posts.title: TypeScript 7 Beta Now Enabled by Default in Visual Studio 2026 18.6 Insiders 3
recent_posts.summary: Visual Studio 2026 18.6 Insiders 3 now ships with TypeScript 7 Beta (native preview) as the default built-in TypeScript SDK. The native port of the TypeScript compiler delivers up to 10x faster compile times and ~8x faster project load times through native execution and shared-memory parallelism. The update affects all projects using the built-in SDK, including TypeScript, JavaScript, and ASP.NET Core projects. Users can revert to the previous language service via Tools > Options > Preview Features, or pin to TypeScript 6.x or a specific native preview version via npm. Several known issues exist including missing quick fixes, incomplete Find All References, broken file rename import updates, and JSDoc auto-generation not working.

recent_posts.title: SDK-Style Support for Extension Projects
recent_posts.summary: Visual Studio 18.5 introduces official SDK-style project support for VSSDK-based extension (VSIX) projects. The update brings up to 75% build time reduction through incremental build support and Fast Up-To-Date Check, updated in-box templates defaulting to SDK-style, and a more compact csproj format. Existing MPF-style extensions continue to work without forced migration. A migration guide covers key steps including XAML support, solution deployment configuration, and key MSBuild properties. Microsoft is also experimenting with an agentic conversion workflow via the vs-agent-plugins Modernize agent.

recent_posts.title: Visual Studio April Update – Cloud Agent Integration
recent_posts.summary: Visual Studio's April 2026 update focuses on deeper GitHub Copilot agent integration. Key additions include cloud agent sessions that run on remote infrastructure and create pull requests autonomously, user-level custom agents stored in a personal directory that travel across projects, C++ code editing tools for agent mode now generally available (with class and call hierarchy navigation), and a new Debugger Agent that validates bug fixes against live runtime behavior. Smaller UX improvements include IntelliSense now taking priority over Copilot completions to reduce distraction, and customizable keyboard shortcuts for accepting inline suggestions.

recent_posts.title: From AI to .NET: 20 VS Live! Las Vegas Sessions You Can Watch Now
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has published 20 sessions from VS Live! Las Vegas 2026 on the Visual Studio YouTube channel, releasing approximately two per day. Topics covered include AI-assisted development with GitHub Copilot, modern .NET and C#, cloud-native apps on Azure, developer productivity, and real-world architecture. Notable sessions include keynotes on Visual Studio 2027 and AI applications, plus talks on ASP.NET Core, GitHub Actions, caching in .NET, and VS Code integration. Upcoming in-person VS Live! events are scheduled through 2027, with discounts available for Visual Studio subscribers.

recent_posts.title: Stop Hunting Bugs: Meet the New Visual Studio Debugger Agent
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft is introducing a new Debugger Agent workflow in Visual Studio that transforms debugging from a manual, guesswork-heavy process into a guided, AI-powered loop. The agent connects to the live runtime, proposes root cause hypotheses, sets intelligent breakpoints, monitors runtime state during bug reproduction, validates findings in real time, and proposes verified fixes. The feature is available in Visual Studio 18.5 GA, initially optimized for exceptions, logic inconsistencies, and state corruption scenarios, with plans to expand automation further.

recent_posts.title: Take full control of your floating windows in Visual Studio
recent_posts.summary: Visual Studio has a little-known setting under Tools > Options > Environment > Windows > Floating Windows that controls how floating tool windows and documents behave. The dropdown offers three modes: None, Tool Windows (default), and Documents and Tool Windows. Setting it to None makes floating windows fully independent — they get their own taskbar entries, stay visible when the main IDE is minimized, and don't force themselves to the front. This pairs especially well with PowerToys FancyZones for custom multi-monitor layouts, letting developers snap Visual Studio windows into zones like any normal application window.

recent_posts.title: Bookmark Studio: evolving bookmarks in Visual Studio
recent_posts.summary: Bookmark Studio is a new experimental Visual Studio extension that enhances the built-in bookmarks feature. It adds slot-based navigation (Alt+Shift+1-9 shortcuts for direct bookmark access), a dedicated Bookmark Manager tool window with filtering and search, optional organization via labels, colors, and folders, and export capabilities to plain text, Markdown, or CSV for sharing with teammates or in pull requests. Bookmarks also track text movement during editing to stay attached to the correct code lines. The extension is available on the Visual Studio Marketplace.

recent_posts.title: Visual Studio March 2026 update adds custom Copilot agents and profiling tools
recent_posts.summary: Visual Studio's March 2026 update introduces several GitHub Copilot enhancements. Custom agents can now be defined as `.agent.md` files in your repository, letting teams build specialized Copilot agents with access to workspace tools, preferred models, and MCP connections. Agent skills provide reusable instruction sets picked up automatically from repository directories. A new `find_symbol` tool gives agent mode language-aware symbol navigation across C++, C#, Razor, and TypeScript codebases. Enterprise MCP governance lets admins enforce allowlists for MCP servers. On the diagnostics side, a new 'Profile with Copilot' command in Test Explorer automates test profiling, and inline perf tips during debugging surface optimization suggestions in real time. Copilot can also fix NuGet vulnerabilities directly from Solution Explorer. Additionally, HTML rich copy/cut now preserves syntax highlighting when pasting code into external applications.

recent_posts.title: Syncfusion UI components and SDKs now included in Visual Studio subscriptions
recent_posts.summary: Visual Studio subscribers (Professional, Enterprise, and Dev Essentials) can access Syncfusion tools at no additional cost. Benefits include 1,600+ UI components for .NET, JavaScript, XAML, MAUI, and Blazor; document processing SDKs for PDF, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; Bold BI for embedded analytics dashboards; and BoldSign for e-signature API integration. Professional and Enterprise subscribers get 12 months of the Essential Studio Enterprise Edition, while Dev Essentials members receive 6 months of the UI Edition plus ongoing access to 20 developer eBooks. Redistribution of libraries or sharing license keys is not permitted.

recent_posts.title: Visual Studio subscriptions monthly newsletter now available for opt-in
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has launched a monthly email newsletter for Visual Studio Professional and Enterprise subscribers to help them discover and use the full range of benefits included in their subscriptions. Many subscribers are unaware of perks like monthly Azure credits, Azure Dev/Test pricing, training platforms (Pluralsight, Cloud Academy), event discounts, and partner offers. The newsletter aims to deliver concise, actionable updates including insider tips, coupon codes, event announcements, and benefit explanations directly to subscribers' inboxes once a month.

top_posts.title: Visual Studio 2026 launches with performance improvements and AI integration
top_posts.summary: Visual Studio 2026 is now generally available with significant performance improvements, including 50% fewer UI hangs and faster startup times. The release introduces AI-native features through GitHub Copilot integration, including new C# and C++ agents for debugging, profiling, and app modernization. Over 5,000 bugs were fixed and 300 feature requests implemented based on community feedback. The IDE now decouples from build tools, allowing updates without affecting .NET or C++ compilers, and maintains full compatibility with Visual Studio 2022 projects and over 4,000 extensions.

top_posts.title: Using GitHub Copilot to complete three postponed development projects
top_posts.summary: A developer shares their experience using GitHub Copilot and AI agents in Visual Studio to complete three long-postponed projects during a holiday weekend: converting a book into a static website, building a TOON language parser and Visual Studio extension, and creating new color themes. The AI tools provided 5-10x speed improvements by generating code, handling isolated tasks in parallel, and jumpstarting complex work. While AI accelerated development significantly, manual refinement and traditional coding were still needed for certain tasks. The experience demonstrates how AI coding assistants can overcome procrastination by reducing the initial barrier to starting overwhelming projects.

top_posts.title: Visual Studio 2026 Insiders is here!
top_posts.summary: Microsoft announces Visual Studio 2026 Insiders, featuring deeply integrated AI capabilities, significant performance improvements for enterprise-scale development, and a modern UI redesign using Fluent UI. The release introduces the new Insiders Channel replacing the Preview Channel, includes GitHub Copilot Free integration, and promises faster solution loading, building, and debugging across both x64 and Arm64 architectures. The IDE now offers enhanced code understanding, automated testing suggestions, performance profiling with AI-powered fixes, and 11 new color themes.

top_posts.title: Making Visual Studio a bit more visual
top_posts.summary: Developers frequently work with various image references in their code, but the string values don't show the actual images. A new feature in Visual Studio introduces an editor tooltip that previews images when hovered over, showing the original size capped at 500 pixels, along with the image's dimensions and file size. This feature currently supports common file types like PNG, JPG, and WebP, among others. Experiment feedback has led to the ability to click for a full view in an external viewer, while features like zoom are considered for future updates. Available in Visual Studio 2022 v17.10 or newer.

top_posts.title: Visual Studio UI Refresh
top_posts.summary: The Microsoft Fluent design language provides a unified framework to create and deliver more productive, consistent, and accessible applications. The current visual language (which hasn’t been updated since Visual Studio 2012) has limitations for many customers. The new UI updates focus on three main pillars: cohesiveness, accessibility, and productivity.
